title: Lake Weyba western shore

bikeon.heading: Lake Weyba western shore
paras: The lakeside path at Weyba Downs follows the western shore of Lake Weyba, the southern end of the Noosa Everglades system. The catchment was never fertile enough for farming, so much of the lake still looks as it did to its Kabi Kabi custodians, whose shell middens, scarred trees and a large stone fish trap at the southern end remain. In the 1890s, under the Co-operative Communities Land Settlement Act, 59 unemployed Brisbane men and their families, the Woolloongabba Exemplars, settled the western side. They sold fish to Gympie and Brisbane, but their hand dug wells dried up and the commune had collapsed by 1896. Eumarella Road takes its name from the Tainsh family property at Rocky Point, a local picnic spot into the 1950s. South of the lake, Murdering Creek is thought to mark a massacre of Aboriginal people in the 1860s; historians have not settled the date or how many died.

story: This quiet western shore of Lake Weyba, the southern end of the Noosa Everglades system, has changed very little. The land was never rich enough to farm, so much of it still looks as it did to its Kabi Kabi custodians. Their shell middens, scarred trees and a large stone fish trap remain.

In the 1890s, under a government scheme, 59 unemployed men from Brisbane and their families tried to make a living on this side of the lake. They were known as the Woolloongabba Exemplars, and they sold fish to Gympie and Brisbane. Their hand dug wells failed, and by 1896 the commune was gone.
South of the lake, Murdering Creek is thought to mark a massacre of Aboriginal people in the 1860s. Historians have not settled the date, or how many died.
